subject: pharmacology
title: Streptomycin in Tuberculosis, Isoniazid Neuropathy, Pyridoxine and Hepatotoxicity Management

steps.tx: **Streptomycin**, tuberculosis' first effective drug (1943) and its first resistance lesson (monotherapy relapsed resistant within months, inventing combination therapy), is an intramuscular aminoglycoside now demoted to reserve roles by its oto and nephrotoxicity, injection burden and the oral era. It survives in defined drug resistant regimens historically, plague, tularaemia and brucellosis partnerships, and in examinations as the aminoglycoside whose vestibular toxicity named the class effect.
steps.say: Streptomycin cured and relapsed tuberculosis in one trial and thereby invented combination therapy.

steps.tx: **Peripheral neuropathy** is isoniazid's signature: the drug inactivates pyridoxine (vitamin B6) by hydrazone formation and inhibits its activation, starving glutamic acid decarboxylase and axonal maintenance, producing distal symmetrical sensory neuropathy (and, rarely, seizures from GABA failure). Slow acetylators, diabetics, alcohol use, pregnancy, HIV, renal failure and malnutrition stack risk. It is preventable entirely by co prescribed pyridoxine, which is negligence law in tablet form where omitted in risk groups.
steps.say: Isoniazid steals vitamin B6 and nerves pay; pyridoxine beside it is not optional in risk groups.

nodes.label: Active B6 falls, GABA synthesis threatened

steps.tx: The hydrazine group of isoniazid binds vitamin B6 as a hydrazone and blocks activation of what remains. Long sensory axons fail first. The result is a **distal neuropathy**, burning and numbness in the feet, commoner in slow acetylators, diabetes, pregnancy, alcohol use and malnutrition. A seizure from loss of GABA is the rare central form of the same failure. A small daily dose of pyridoxine prevents it. Omitting that tablet in a person at risk is the preventable error.
steps.say: Isoniazid inactivates pyridoxine by forming a hydrazone, and the feet go numb. Slow acetylators, diabetes, pregnancy and malnutrition raise the risk. A small daily dose of pyridoxine prevents the neuropathy.

vis.alt: Isoniazid forming a hydrazone with pyridoxine, with distal sensory loss in the feet.
vis.caption: Isoniazid binds pyridoxine as a hydrazone, and sensation is lost first in the long nerves of the feet. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Pyridoxine** dosing is bidirectional teaching: prophylaxis at 10 to 25 mg daily in risk groups (higher in some HIV and pregnancy protocols), treatment of established neuropathy at larger divided doses while isoniazid continues where possible, and gram scale pyridoxine as the antidote to isoniazid overdose seizures (equal grams to the isoniazid ingested, infused slowly, with benzodiazepines bridging because diazepam needs B6 to work). Excess pyridoxine itself causes sensory neuropathy, closing the loop examiners love.
steps.say: Ten milligrams prevents, grams rescue overdose seizures, and chronic excess causes the very neuropathy it treats.

left.title: Pyridoxine prophylaxis and treatment
points: 10 to 25 mg daily with isoniazid in risk groups
Risk: diabetes, alcohol, pregnancy, HIV, renal failure
Neuropathy treatment: higher doses, isoniazid reviewed
Breastfed infants of treated mothers supplemented

right.title: Pyridoxine as antidote
points: Isoniazid overdose seizures refractory to diazepam alone
Grams equal to isoniazid ingested, slow infusion

steps.tx: **Hepatotoxicity** across the regimen was sequenced previously; here the fingerprints separate: isoniazid causes hepatocellular necrosis (hydrazine metabolites, age gradient, alcohol, rifampicin induction multiplying toxic metabolites in the famous synergy of injury), rifampicin adds cholestatic and competitive bilirubin uptake elevation (transient hyperbilirubinaemia without injury), and pyrazinamide contributes dose related hepatocellular damage that historically removed it from American regimens for a generation.
steps.say: Isoniazid injures hepatocytes, rifampicin colours bilirubin, pyrazinamide doses the liver; read the pattern before stopping all three.

left.title: Hepatocellular culprits
points: Isoniazid: metabolite necrosis, age and alcohol risk
Pyrazinamide: dose related, intensive phase window

steps.tx: **Isoniazid's wider adverse** and interaction set completes its portrait: lupus like syndrome in slow acetylators, euphoria and psychosis rarely, gynaecomastia, and CYP inhibition raising phenytoin and carbamazepine toward toxicity (the mirror of rifampicin's induction in the same regimen, a combination that keeps pharmacists employed). MAO and histaminase inhibition explain tyramine and histamine fish (skipjack) reactions counselled in older texts.
steps.say: Isoniazid inhibits where rifampicin induces; phenytoin caught between them needs levels.

nodes.label: Rifampicin induction pulls the opposite way
Phenytoin levels arbitrate the tug of war

steps.tx: **Streptomycin's aminoglycoside monitoring** from the previous module applies unchanged and harder: baseline and serial audiometry where courses lengthen, vestibular enquiry (oscillopsia, imbalance) at every visit, renal dose spacing, pregnancy prohibition (congenital deafness), and cumulative dose ceilings respected across a treatment lifetime that may span relapses. Its modern reserve use is specialist signed for exactly these reasons.
steps.say: Streptomycin courses carry audiograms and dose ledgers; pregnancy forbids it outright.

left.title: Monitoring bundle
points: Creatinine and dose spacing by kidney function
Stop at first vestibular complaint, not the last

steps.tx: **Second line injectables** inherited streptomycin's chair and its toxicities: amikacin and kanamycin (with capreomycin, a polypeptide, beside them) anchored MDR regimens for decades at the cost of deafness wards, until all oral bedaquiline regimens (next lessons) displaced them from guidelines between 2019 and 2022. Their fall is the module's happiest pharmacology revision and examinations now test the displacement as much as the drugs.
steps.say: Injectables deafened a generation of MDR patients; oral regimens retired them within three guideline years.

left.title: Injectable era (to about 2019)
points: Amikacin, kanamycin or capreomycin daily injections
Hearing loss in a substantial minority
Success barely half in many cohorts

right.title: All oral era
points: Audiometry burden lifted with the injections

steps.tx: **Patient counselling for** the standard regimen compresses this and the previous lesson into adherence saving sentences: orange urine is rifampicin and harmless, numb feet are isoniazid and preventable if reported early, yellow eyes stop everything and phone today, contraception and other medicines must be re argued with the team, and finishing month six after feeling cured at month two is where relapses and resistance are prevented.
steps.say: Orange is fine, numbness is early, yellow is urgent, and month six is the cure month two promises.

nodes.label: Numb feet: report early, pyridoxine reviewed
Jaundice or vomiting: stop and contact same day
Completion at month 6 prevents relapse and resistance
